In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for some residues, there is a systematic variation of the relative populations of the chi1 rotameric states with resolution, which is a consequence of the presence of dual occupancy at low resolutions.
the systematic variation of chi1 mean values with crystallographic resolution is a consequence of multiple chi1 states.
the systematic variations in chi 1 rotamer populations with resolution are consistent with the hypothesis that they represent the presence of dual rotameric occupancy at low resolution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the systematic variation in mean chi1 rotamer populations with resolution, which is observed for a number of residues, may be accounted for by a change in the relative populations of rotamers with resolution.

the chi1 side chain conformation in protein crystal structures varies systematically with resolution, and that this variation can be accounted for as a consequence of dual occupancy of multiple chi1 rotameric states at low resolution.

, at least for some residues, there are two or more conformations in equilibrium in the crystal, with the equilibrium being perturbed by the crystal environment to a greater or lesser extent depending on the residue type, and the resolution of the data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chi 1 torsion angle is not a binary variable, but a continuous variable that can take on multiple states.
the chi 1 side-chain torsions in proteins are not as simple as previously assumed.
the conformational preferences of side-chains can be affected by the resolution of the crystallographic data.
